violations.text: -Cooked beef tenderloin, meatballs and rice were observed held at 45-48 degrees Fahrenheit. Hot chicken was observed cooling under foods. PIC voluntarily decided to disposed of food as corrective action. -Cream cheese and butter were observed held at 53 degrees Fahrenheit. Cold holding unit was observed off during time of inspection. Unit was turned on. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Cooked sausage was observed at 102 degrees Fahrenheit in omelet prep unit. Food was placed onto shallow pan and placed into walk-in cooler to blast chill. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

The following were observed in poor repair: -hoses in dishroom (held together with black tape) -conveyor belt at clean dishes side (held together with duct tape) -cutting board in The Grill (heavily scored and scratched) New Violation. Correct By: 09/19/2026
Several floor tiles by the kettles were observed in poor repair. Equipment to be in good repair and proper adjustment. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 05/23/2025

The walls behind and around 3 bay sink in The Grill are in poor repair. The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. Materials for wall surfaces shall be smooth, durable, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent for areas subject to moisture such as food preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, ware-washing areas, and toilet rooms. New Violation. Correct By: 09/19/2026

The kitchen hoods and vents in The Grill and above kettles in main kitchen area have an accumulation of soil residue and food debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 08/19/2026

Lexans of pasta were observed stored in containers greater than 4 inches deep, stacked and covered. Food was observed at 70 degrees Fahrenheit. Foods were separated into smaller containers and placed with ice during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 04/23/2025

The following were observed in poor repair: 1. lexan food containers and lids 2. hot holding cabinet (parts on order per PIC) Equipment to be in good repair and proper adjustment. New Violation. Correct By: 05/23/2025
Several floor tiles by the kettles were observed in poor repair. Equipment to be in good repair and proper adjustment. New Violation. Correct By: 05/23/2025
Food container lids in the walk-in cooler observed cracked/chipped. Equipment shall be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 10/13/2023

The non-food contact surfaces of the vent in the ware-washing room have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. The non-food contact surfaces shall be cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup of residue. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2023

Inadequate lighting observed in the walk-in cooler.Lighting 6-303.11 Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning. -Lighting levels are specified so that sufficient light is available to enable employees to perform certain functions such as reading labels; discerning the color of substances; identifying toxic materials; recognizing the condition of food, utensils, and supplies; and safely conducting general food establishment operations and clean-up. Properly distributed light makes the need for cleaning apparent by making accumulations of soil conspicuous. New Violation. Correct By: 10/27/2023
